analysis:
Compared all supplied base/head integration-test source, file metadata and bounded patches. CoordinatorIntegrationTests.swift adds loopback tests for rapid reconnection following close code 1012 (head 456–472), stable-session backoff reset (474–490), policy injection (649–676), and bounded re-registration helpers (679–727). Existing encryption, cancellation/reservation release, attestation transport, enrollment signature, catalog, telemetry and update-banner assertions remain unchanged. These test-only changes do not establish a new authorization bypass, plaintext disclosure, billing manipulation or privileged-helper/cache regression against the indexed model. Fake attestation signatures remain explicitly transport fixtures, not evidence of serving permission.
The visible patch for CoordinatorReconnectPolicyTests.swift checks reset after sessions of at least 60 seconds and subsequent backoff growth; only part of this added 95-line file is supplied. CI participation is described at integration-test head 10–12, but the runner/workflow is not supplied here.
Integration must verify the production CoordinatorReconnectPolicy and CoordinatorClient runLoop changes behind these tests: close-code propagation, delay growth/reset and cancellation under repeated reconnects (TB-002 availability), plus preservation of connection invalidation, origin-bound outbound delivery and fresh authorization across reconnects (TB-011, T-053, A-016). Faster registration must not be mistaken for restored serving permission. The unchanged tests only verify re-registration and legacy challenge delivery, not these authorization contracts. Missing runtime source and the truncated new test patch are coverage limits, not proof of a regression or of safety; runtime security conclusions remain unresolved for integration.
